````markdown
# Generating Release Notes

## Steps

1. Find the last release tag: `git describe --tags --abbrev=0`
2. Collect commits since it: `git log <tag>..HEAD --oneline`
3. Group commits by conventional-commit type prefix; each group becomes a section.
4. Write the result to `RELEASE_NOTES.md` at the repo root.

## Commit type mapping

| Commit type | Section |
|-------------|---------|
| `feat` | Features |
| `fix` | Bug Fixes |
| `perf` | Performance |
| `docs`, `chore`, `ci`, `build` | omit |
| `refactor` | omit unless user-facing |
| `revert` | Reverts; also remove the reverted entry if it is in the same release |
| any type with `!` (e.g. `feat!`) | Breaking Changes |
| `fix(security)` or any security scope | Security |

## Output rules

- Section order: Breaking Changes, Security, Features, Performance, Bug Fixes, Reverts.
- Omit empty sections.
- Every entry links its PR number as `[#123]`. If a commit has no PR number, flag it to the user instead of inventing one.
- Entries are one line, imperative mood, no trailing period.
````
